chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah said:

I asked him about a woman who dies before her husband consummates the marriage with her, or the husband dies before he consummates the marriage with her. He said: 'Whichever of them dies, the woman is entitled to half of what was prescribed for her. And if no dowry was prescribed for her, then she has no dowry.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the dowry if the husband or wife dies before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the financial rights of the wife in cases of death prior to consummation (*dukhul*), establishing that half the stipulated dowry is due as a debt against the deceased's estate. This ruling aligns with the principle that the marriage contract is fully effective even without physical union, distinguishing it from the case of divorce before consummation. It underscores the legal continuity of the marital bond in Shia jurisprudence regarding inheritance and financial obligations.
